note.explanation: Personal protective equipment (PPE) helps students face emergencies in the laboratory and reduces exposure to hazardous chemicals. Your textbook lists lab coats, protective glasses, face shields, aprons, boots and hearing protection as PPE.
examples: Protective glasses are an example of PPE.
A lab coat is another example of PPE.
note.checkAnswer: PPE helps students face emergencies and reduces exposure to hazardous chemicals.
note.simple: PPE is protective clothing or equipment used in the lab to help keep students safe.

note.title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
steps: Recognise situations in which protective equipment may be needed.
Make suitable PPE available to students.
Use items such as lab coats and protective glasses to help reduce exposure to hazards.
note.answer: Examples include a lab coat and protective glasses.

options: Equipment used to protect people in the laboratory
A chemical used to clean laboratory benches
A label placed on a chemical bottle
A device used only to measure temperature
mcqs.stem: What does PPE mean in the context of laboratory safety?
rationales: Correct: PPE means personal protective equipment used to help protect people.
Incorrect: Cleaning chemicals are not what the term PPE means.
Incorrect: A bottle label is not protective equipment.
Incorrect: A thermometer measures temperature and is not PPE.

options: To reduce exposure to hazardous chemicals
To identify the chemical in a bottle
mcqs.stem: According to the section, PPE is useful because it can:
rationales: Correct: The section says PPE is useful to reduce exposure to hazardous chemicals.
Incorrect: The section does not say PPE changes the speed of a reaction.
Incorrect: PPE does not replace instructions.
Incorrect: Chemical identification is not given as the purpose of PPE.

mcqs.stem: Which item is listed as PPE in the section?
rationales: Correct: A lab coat is listed as an item of protective equipment.
Incorrect: A measuring cylinder is laboratory apparatus, not an item listed as PPE.
Incorrect: A test tube rack holds test tubes and is not listed as PPE.
Incorrect: A chemical bottle stores chemicals and is not PPE.

mcqs.stem: Which item can protect a student's eyes and is named in the section?
rationales: Correct: Protective glasses are named in the section and protect the eyes.
Incorrect: A filter funnel is used to pour or filter substances, not to protect the eyes.
Incorrect: A dropper transfers small amounts of liquid and is not eye protection.
Incorrect: An evaporating dish is laboratory apparatus, not eye protection.

mcqs.stem: Which of these is listed as protective equipment?
rationales: Correct: A face shield is specifically listed as PPE.
Incorrect: A beaker is used to hold substances and is not listed as PPE.
Incorrect: A spatula is used to handle small amounts of solids, not as PPE.
Incorrect: A stirring rod is used for stirring and is not PPE.

mcqs.stem: Which item of PPE is named in the section?
rationales: Correct: Hearing protection is included in the section's list of PPE.
Incorrect: A thermometer measures temperature and is not listed as PPE.
Incorrect: A tripod stand supports apparatus and is not PPE.
Incorrect: A wash bottle is laboratory equipment, not PPE.

explain.title: Why PPE is needed
explain.body: Personal protective equipment should be made available to students to face any emergency situation which may arise in the lab. They are also useful to reduce exposures to hazardous chemicals.

explain.title: Examples of PPE
explain.body: Proper protective equipment include such items as lab coat, protective glasses, face shields, apron, boots and hearing protection.

explain.title: How to remember the purpose
explain.body: Remember two purposes: PPE can help students face laboratory emergencies and can reduce their exposure to hazardous chemicals.

mistakes: Do not confuse PPE with laboratory apparatus such as beakers or measuring cylinders.
Do not give only one example when the question asks you to name several items.
Do not forget the purpose of PPE: facing emergencies and reducing exposure to hazardous chemicals.
Use the textbook's exact item names where possible.
